title: Opportunistic coalescing and tail smoothing for embedding endpoint latency
creator: Lin Zhao
description: Background: Production embedding workloads show a long right tail at p99 for single-embedding and small-batch requests. Existing micro-batching decreases cost but creates fragmentation when request arrival patterns are spiky (short bursts of 1-4 requests). Goal: reduce tail latency without regressing median latency or increasing token-level cost materially. Approach: implement an opportunistic coalescing layer in the embedding front-end that merges near-simultaneous tiny requests into transient coalesced batches, combined with a small tail-aware kernel tuning (dynamic kernel selection and preferred CUDA stream ordering) and a short speculative execution path for stale KV cache misses. This ticket scopes the prototype, profiling, correctness checks, and canary rollout plan.
observed_baseline: Current p50/p95/p99 for single-embedding API: 6ms / 22ms / 135ms. Under 99th burst traffic observed p99 jumps to ~220ms. Cost uplift when forcing larger batches is ~+8% token-unit equivalent due to padding and model kernel shape inefficiencies.
acceptance_criteria: p99 for production single-embedding traffic reduced by >=35% relative to baseline (target <=88ms)
no regression on p50 (<=10% relative increase) and p95 (<=5% relative increase)
end-to-end cost per 1k embeddings change <= +3% compared to baseline
feature gated with runtime flag and observable telemetry exposed in Console
automated unit and integration tests for coalescer correctness (ordering, batching semantics) and kernel fallbacks
canary rollout plan and rollback criteria documented

progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Spike completed - proof-of-concept coalescer implemented in local runtime build; basic correctness validated against replay tool
2026-02-27: Offline replay (24h) shows median unchanged, p99 down ~28% for microburst traces; identified kernel hotpath that increases latency when batch shapes are highly asymmetric
2026-03-03: Added kernel selector prototype that prefers narrow-kernel for asymmetric batches; p99 improved further in replay (~38% reduction on target traces)
2026-03-08: Integration tests added; found a race in cancellation path when coalesced batch is dispatched while a caller cancels — patch in review
2026-03-10: Canary plan approved by SRE and PM; telemetry dashboard template created; PR for coalescer merged to canary branch pending infra deploy
tech_notes: Coalescer heuristics: hold-window default 2ms, exponential backoff to avoid starvation; size cap 16 to limit padding overhead
Kernel selector: use batch shape fingerprint (batch_size x seq_len) to map to kernel candidate and a cost heuristic (expected vs worst-case latency)
Speculative path: for KV-cache-miss heavy flows, run light-weight prefix-only kernel while waiting for heavier kernel to warm cache; fallback ensures correctness
Instrumentation: increment counters for coalesced_batches, single_shot_pass, hold_window_expire, kernel_fallbacks. Histogram buckets for end-to-end latency (1ms bins up to 1s).
Replay methodology: use 7-day edge logs; maintain arrival timestamps and request metadata; replay at 1x and 5x to stress scheduler; compare lat metrics per-client and globally
Safety: ordering preserved by tagging requests in coalesced batch and restoring original order on response assemble; cancellation propagates explicit token to coalescer queue
perf_results_snapshot: Replay 24h (3/01 revision): p50 6.2ms (baseline 6ms), p95 21.0ms (baseline 22ms), p99 82ms (baseline 135ms) on sampled microburst workload; cost proxy +1.7%
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Increased padding for heterogenous sequence lengths could increase cost - mitigation: cap coalescer size and prefer fold-by-length heuristic
Risk: Cancellation race can drop responses - mitigation: integrate strict ACK path and add unit tests; observed race fixed in patch 16786-rc1
Risk: Kernel selection adds schedule jitter - mitigation: keep selection fast (table lookup) and fall back to default kernel under high load
qa_plan: Unit tests covering assembly ordering, cancellation, and error propagation
Integration test harness with synthetic spike generator (1ms inter-arrival bursts)
Replay validation against production A/B bucket comparing contextual quality and latency
Manual load test on dedicated-embed-pool-3 with SRE observing telemetry
